result:
The value is $m(k,k)=(k^{k-1}+k-1)^2$. I verified that this value is achieved by an explicit construction, but I did not prove the matching upper bound, so that part rests on the claim that the optimum for large $k$ is attained by this type of construction.

**Construction.** Take disjoint sets:
- $V_1,\dots,V_{k-1}$, each of size $k$ (so $V_i=\{p_{i,1},\dots,p_{i,k}\}$);
- $E_1,\dots,E_{k-1}$, each of size $k$, with $E_j=\{p_{1,j},\dots,p_{k-1,j},x_j\}$ (the $x_j$ are new points);
- a point $z$, not in any of the above.

Let $\mathrm{Tr}(\cdot)$ denote the transversals (one point chosen from each set), and set

- $\mathcal F=\{T\cup\{z\}: T\in \mathrm{Tr}(V_1,\dots,V_{k-1})\}\cup\{E_1,\dots,E_{k-1}\}$, so $|\mathcal F|=k^{k-1}+k-1$;
- $\mathcal G=\{\{z\}\cup R: R\in \mathrm{Tr}(E_1,\dots,E_{k-1})\}\cup\{V_1,\dots,V_{k-1}\}$, so $|\mathcal G|=k^{k-1}+k-1$.

**Cross-intersection.**
- $T\cup\{z\}$ meets $\{z\}\cup R$ at $z$, and meets $V_i$ since $T$ contains a point of $V_i$.
- $E_j$ meets $\{z\}\cup R$ since $R$ contains a point of $E_j$, and meets $V_i$ at $p_{i,j}$.

**Covering numbers.**
- $\tau(\mathcal F)=k$: a $(k-1)$-set $S$ either contains $z$, in which case the remaining $\le k-2$ points cannot hit the $k-1$ pairwise disjoint sets $E_j$; or it does not, in which case some transversal of the $V_i$ avoids $S$ because each $V_i$ has $k$ points. Covering by $V_1$ (or any $V_i$) uses $k$ points, so $\tau(\mathcal F)=k$.
- $\tau(\mathcal G)=k$: the same argument applies with the roles of the $V_i$ and $E_j$ exchanged.

So this pair gives $|\mathcal F||\mathcal G|=(k^{k-1}+k-1)^2$, which matches the proposed value. (As a check, $k=2$ gives $9$, which agrees with the triangle construction.)

ANSWER: $(k^{k-1}+k-1)^2$
